subject: red Amazon ant
title: These Ants Can't Feed Themselves, So They Kidnap Other Ants to Do It

scenes.text: These ants can't feed themselves. So they steal babies.
Amazon ants. Their jaws are curved daggers: perfect for piercing, useless for food or babies.
So on summer afternoons, a column marches out to raid a nest of ordinary wood ants.
They storm it and carry home the pupae. Those hatch in the raiders' nest and spend their lives feeding and cleaning their captors.
The captives outnumber their masters up to ten to one. The masters do nothing but fight.
It starts with one queen. She walks into a stranger's nest, bites and licks their queen for 25 minutes, kills her, and wears her scent. The workers accept her in seconds.

description:
Amazon ants (Polyergus) are obligate slave-makers: their dagger-like jaws cannot handle food or brood, so they survive by raiding Formica ant nests in the afternoon and carrying off pupae, which hatch and then feed, clean and raise young for their captors.
Host workers outnumber Polyergus five to ten to one. A new Polyergus queen invades a Formica nest, bites and licks the resident queen for about 25 minutes, kills her, takes on her scent, and the workers accept her within seconds.
Would you call this slavery or parasitism? Comment below.
first_comment: Raids happen in mid to late afternoon, after the hottest part of the day, and raiders sometimes hit the same nest twice in one afternoon. Which insect society should we cover next?
